given: a stock record whose batch_number and serial_number are both NULL (a code that did not parse during the migration)
when: an API client fetches that stock record
then: the response includes the batch_number and serial_number fields both present and explicitly null, not omitted and not substituted with a combined string

independence.rationale: AC1 and AC2 assert value-bearing rows expose their fields; this AC asserts the null-handling outcome for unparsed rows. An implementation that returns values but omits null fields (or renders them as an empty/combined string) passes AC1/AC2 yet fails here, so it is independently breakable.

architectural_notes: API/boundary AC asserting the null-serialization contract on the stock endpoint (app/routes/). Rests on PI2 (batch_number/serial_number NULLABLE at the schema) so unparsed legacy rows persist as NULL through app/repositories/ and app/services/; the boundary serializer must emit the keys with explicit null rather than dropping them or substituting a combined string. Owner module: the stock response serializer — the null-handling policy lives here, not in the domain. Cross-cutting concern: response contract / null-shape stability, owned by the API layer; verified by an R4 real-branch test that seeds a NULL-tracking row (the client 'not tracked' render is S3/NFR-F6-8, out of this AC's scope).
